Hi all, 

I am conducting measurement invariance and would like to conduct chi square difference tests to see if the model fits (e.g., configural, metric, and scalar) differ from one level of invariance to the next. Hence, I used the lavTestLRT function. 

I used the estimator "MLM" when conducting my CFAs and need some help with deciding which method I should use ("satorra.bentler.2001", "satorra.bentler.2010"). Is there a difference between the two? 

Thank you.

Kind regards,
Joan

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Chi Square Difference Tests for Measurement Invariance
parts: deciding which method I should use ("satorra.bentler.2001", "satorra.bentler.2010"). Is there a difference between the two?

From the ?lavTestLRT help page:

  • If method is "satorra.bentler.2001", a simple approximation is used described in Satorra & Bentler (2001). In some settings, this can lead to a negative test statistic. To ensure a positive test statistic, we can use the method proposed by Satorra & Bentler (2010).
So just use 2010 if the 2001 method returns a negative statistic.  Otherwise, they should be equivalent (at least asymptotically).
